newsitem.title: USA: IMCO Recycling to close Calif plant.
newsitem.headline: IMCO Recycling to close Calif plant.

text.p: IMCO Recycling Inc said Thursday it decided to close its California aluminum recycling plant and speed up the closure of the first cell of a company-owned landfill in Morgantown, Kentucy.
The company said it hoped that by eliminating the losses put up by the California plant, it would improve its future results.
President and Chief Executive Frank Romanelli said in a statement that the California plant was closed because it "has operated far below capacity and has recorded losses throughout 1996."
Although operating efficiency has improved at the facility, Romanelli said "demand for export aluminum from the Far East, the plant's largest market, has virtually disappeared."
The company said it did not believe that drop in demand was likely to change any time soon.
It did not give a reason or time table for the closing of the first cell of its landfill in Kentucky.
The company did not immediately return a telephone call seeking more information.

A company spokesman said later Thursday morning that the first cell in the Kentucky landfill was originally going to close in the middle of next year. It now is expected to close by the end of this year, he said.
The cell has been in operation since 1990. The company is in the middle of plans to expand a second cell at the landfill.
